transcript: If you were not at Queen of Versailles last night for Sheron A. Scott's debut in the title role, I genuinely feel bad for you. This was one of the most transcendent theater experiences I have ever had, and it's really a testament to how a performer can transform a show just with their performance. Sherry's Jackie is very different from Kristen's. Kristen's Jackie feels like she is trying to will you into liking this character despite the fact that you know that you shouldn't. Whereas Sherry, I don't think, makes any attempt to make you like this character. She is completely dead behind the eyes, incredibly vapid. I would describe her performance as like Anna Faris mixed with a real housewife. And it really shifts the tone of the show in a way that I think is much more in line with what the creatives originally intended. I think it's also worth noting that we saw the show in basically a full theater of people there excited to see Sherry and to give Sherry and the rest of the cast so much energy. This was their first performance back since finding out that the show is going to be closing in January. And I was really glad for the cast that they had such an energetic crowd. And theater being such a communal experience, being in an audience that is that engaged, I think really enhanced the show as well. And so a combination of the audience and seeing Sherry give this incredible debut performance that completely reinvents this role and the show made it one of the most memorable theater experiences of the year for me. I still don't think that this is a perfect show, but it is far from the dumpster fire that some people try to make it out to be. And especially with Sherry at the helm, I think it is well worth your time. She only has two more performances on December 3rd, so if you are free that day, I highly recommend to go see Sherry, Rene Scott, and Queen of Versailles. I really don't think you'll be disappointed.
